findings.evidence: FIX chase-outage-fee-reversal introText p2: 'A bank fee reversal is a customer request decided at the discretion of Chase, not an automatic legal right.' -> 'The checked sources do not show a Chase policy that reverses fees for this outage, so treat each reversal as a request to Chase.' FIX faqs[0].answer: 'Chase decides fee reversals on a case-by-case basis at its own discretion.' -> 'The checked sources do not show a Chase policy that guarantees reversals.' FIX Our Takeaway: 'Reversal decisions remain at the discretion of Chase, while a Regulation E error notice serves as a separate legal avenue only if' -> 'The checked sources do not show that Chase must reverse a fee. A Regulation E error notice is a separate route that applies only if'. Also update evidence.json conditions ('Chase has discretion on fee reversal') to match.

FIX chase-outage-fee-reversal Our Takeaway last sentence: 'then read how much cash to keep outside one bank before the next outage' -> 'then read how much emergency fund you need to cover a gap while a bank is down'. If that wording still overreaches, use the plain anchor 'how much emergency fund you need'.

FIX When to Escalate to the CFPB: 'The CFPB intake questionnaire asks whether you reached out to Chase before filing.' -> 'The CFPB complaint guide suggests trying the company first.' and 'Before submitting a complaint, verify that you attempted to resolve the dispute with Chase first.' -> 'Before submitting a complaint, contact Chase first.'

FIX src/data/guides.ts chase-outage-fee-reversal: "tools": [] -> "tools": [{ "label": "emergency fund calculator", "href": "/emergency-fund-calculator/" }] (route is in the site nav). Check the GuideTool shape against a sibling entry.

FIX replace each 'the bank'/'The bank' that refers to Chase with 'Chase' (e.g. 'Chase acknowledged that some transactions were taking longer than normal'; 'Chase must decide within 10 business days whether an error occurred'; 'if Chase leaves the charges in place'). 'The financial institution' inside the Regulation E definition may stay as the regulation's term.

FIX Fortune sentence -> 'In 2010, Chase online banking was down for more than a day. Fortune reports that Chase then agreed to refund late fees to customers who missed payments, if they called to ask.' FIX 'Under 12 CFR 1005.11 , known as Regulation E, an error includes an unauthorized electronic fund transfer, an incorrect electronic fund transfer to or from your account, or the omission of an electronic fund transfer from your periodic statement.' -> 'Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.11) lists the errors it covers. Three are an unauthorized electronic fund transfer, an incorrect transfer to or from your account, and a transfer missing from your periodic statement.' FIX 'Consumers generally cannot file a second complaint regarding the exact same problem, so ensure your initial submission contains all supporting documentation.' -> 'You generally cannot file a second CFPB complaint about the same problem. Put every date, fee and document in the first one.' Vary lengths in the 10-sentence run with one or two short sentences.

FIX append after the sentence: 'Longer periods of 20 business days and 90 days apply to some new accounts and to certain point-of-sale and foreign transfers (12 CFR 1005.11(c)(3)).' Same one-clause addition in the FAQ answer.

Canonical https://www.themodernwallet.com/guides/chase-outage-fee-reversal/ correct, one inbound from how-much-emergency-fund. External links to NBC, Fortune, eCFR, CFPB and Zelle work. The outbound to how-much-emergency-fund uses a mismatched anchor (A1-ANCHOR-EMERGENCY).

Inspected the captured HTML. Fee table renders as a pipe table inside table-wrap, numbered list and bullet lists render. The tools-pills container is empty under a visible 'Tools for this journey' label (A1-EMPTY-TOOLS). No browser screenshot was taken; layout judged from HTML and template CSS.
Every figure traces to a saved source except the discretion claim and the CFPB intake-questionnaire sentence (A1-DISCRETION, A1-CFPB-QUESTIONNAIRE).

Read the full rendered page. Top answer, request script, fee table, Reg E section, FAQ and takeaway agree except that the 'discretion, not a legal right' framing is unsourced and the closing action links to a guide that does not answer 'cash outside one bank'.

Strongest plausible counterexample tested: a fee caused by an incorrect electronic transfer or Chase-side processing error may be recoverable as a Regulation E error or under the deposit agreement, which contradicts 'not an automatic legal right' stated without source. Reg E deadline claims themselves match the eCFR text. See A1-DISCRETION for the exact fix.

Dates, fee amounts and outage timeline are current as of 2026-11-17 saved captures. Two details fail: Regulation E timing is stated as universal 10/45 days while 12 CFR 1005.11(c)(3) allows 20 business days and 90 days in cases such as new accounts; and the CFPB intake-questionnaire sentence has no source (findings A1-REGE-PERIODS, A1-CFPB-QUESTIONNAIRE).

US federal rules only, which the page implies but does not state. Missing the 20/90-day variants (A1-REGE-PERIODS). The page correctly states the sources do not list NSF or late-fee amounts and presents 2010 as precedent only.

The ask-Chase then CFPB escalation path is sourced (CFPB complaint guide, Fortune 2010 precedent). The framing that reversal is at Chase's discretion and 'not an automatic legal right' is not in any saved source (A1-DISCRETION), and the closing link anchor promises 'cash outside one bank' that the destination guide does not say (A1-ANCHOR-EMERGENCY).
